scope: Explicit x64 ERETS/ERETU FRED continuation state

reference.document: Intel SDM 325462-090, ERETS/ERETU and Vol. 3A 8.4.1-8.4.2, including 8.4.2.4 UMONITOR invalidation

implementation.decoder: Appended ERETS/ERETU IDs 1664/1665 without renumbering older IDs. The shared decoder and scanner require 64-bit mode, retain prefixes, expose implicit state registers and classify both as privileged interrupt returns. Bare CLAC remains distinct.
implementation.context: V9 retains all earlier storage and appends FredConfig at 2544, STIBlocked at 2552 and PendingDebug at 2553; size 2560. Only the low two configuration bits change.
implementation.frames: Skip the error-code qword, read exactly five return qwords at RSP+8..47, validate the canonical RIP and saved reserved fields before any state/RAM write, restore the full new RSP without accessing it.
implementation.supervisor: ERETS preserves all segment caches and GS bases, lowers CSL to min(old,saved), restores complete allowed RFLAGS, and publishes STI/NMI/debug state.
implementation.user: ERETU requires CSL=0. Standard 64-bit selector pairs install flat caches without table reads. Other 64-bit pairs share the GDT/LDT and ordered accessed-bit owner. GS.base swaps with the kernel GS-base MSR, UMONITOR state becomes inactive, and low-DPL DS/ES/FS/GS selectors and caches remain valid.
implementation.events: Old TF or saved pending-DB with restored TF sets PendingDebug. Saved SS conditionally unblocks NMI. Every successful return exits with FredReturn status 12 before target or event execution.
implementation.refactor: Descriptor validation, hidden-cache construction and accessed-bit ordering have one private shared owner for frame returns, FRED and existing segment operations. Flat cache writes are shared with fast system transfers.
implementation.compiler: Existing llvm.x86.erets/eretu and NeverC __builtin_ia32_erets/eretu already generate native frame-return instructions. No LLVM or NeverC source change was needed for this slice.
implementation.monitor_ownership: UIRET/ERETU and inherited V8 IRET/SYSRET/SYSEXIT use the same version-aware monitor writer. RETF invalidates only when CPL changes; same-CPL RETF, SYSENTER and NOP preserve it. Earlier state layouts acquire no monitor store.

regressions_fixed: ERETU initially preserved MonitorActive. A specification audit of SDM 8.4.2.4 exposed the missing effect; the added SDK regression failed before the production fix (neverd-monitor-red.log/xml) and passed afterward.
FRED fixtures initially depended on a later .inc declaration; the fixture now constructs its profile independently.
An old NeverD refining-prefix test expected decode refusal, superseded by the new public IDs; ordinary lifting refusal is separately retained and tested.
Generic Capstone tests failed GCC 15 warnings-as-errors on a nullable strcmp and a shadowed local; the equivalent explicit null comparison and distinct loop variable repair these fixtures.

Nonstandard ERETU initially accepted the null SS selector 3 because its caller passed a constant false null predicate. The new rejection case failed before the real selector predicate was passed to the shared stack-descriptor owner. Standard selector-wrap cases remain valid.
environment_notes: /tmp cannot hold compiler temporary files because its per-user quota is exhausted. Builds and final tests use the task-local /mnt/data TMPDIR; earlier unqualified runs with the default temporary directory are retained as failed diagnostics.
Capstone's deliberate x87 child faults use the existing task-local no-core helper to avoid the global Apport handler. No global core-handler change or unrelated temporary-file cleanup was performed.
Physical FRED is unavailable on this host. No CET, hardware transition, page-fault or asynchronous-event execution is claimed.

GoogleTest CapturedStream hardcodes /tmp on Linux, ignoring TMPDIR. gtest-capture.trace proves EDQUOT on its diagnostic writes. private-tmp-runner.py runs under unshare --user --map-root-user --mount, makes the namespace private, and binds task TMPDIR onto /tmp for the two tests only. The no-core helper is loaded after namespace setup.
